description: Managing resources is critical for mission success. Resources include equipment, personnel, vehicles, and base assets.
equipment durability: Equipment degrades over time, especially under high-stress missions. Players must allocate resources to maintain gear. Example: After every mission, roll a d20 for each piece of equipment. On a 1-5, the item requires repairs (costing 10-20% of its value).
supply management: Each mission consumes resources, requiring preparation during downtime. - Consumables: Ammo, rations, medical supplies, and fuel. - Special Equipment: Dimensional stabilizers, hacking tools, or environmental suits.

records.proposedName: Overview of the Unified Crafting System
records.summary: In Multiversal, crafting isnʼt just a downtime activity—itʼs a powerful tool for creativity, survival, and character identity. Whether forging a void-tempered blade, distilling potions from lunar herbs, or modifying a spaceship's engine core, crafting is woven directly into the gameʼs progression systems, economy, and narrative. This section introduces the Unified Crafting System—a flexible framework that governs how all crafting, repairing, enhancing, modifying, and enchanting is handled across every setting and genre.

description: In Multiversal, crafting isnʼt just a downtime activity—itʼs a powerful tool for creativity, survival, and character identity. Whether forging a void-tempered blade, distilling potions from lunar herbs, or modifying a spaceship's engine core, crafting is woven directly into the gameʼs progression systems, economy, and narrative. This section introduces the Unified Crafting System—a flexible framework that governs how all crafting, repairing, enhancing, modifying, and enchanting is handled across every setting and genre.
the crafting formula: At the heart of all crafting disciplines is a shared structure: Materials + Tools + Process + Skill = Final Product Each component influences the itemʼs quality, properties, and success rate: •Materials determine the potential power and rarity of the item. •Tools enable or enhance the crafting process, with higher-quality tools granting bonuses. •Process includes specific steps, rolls, and checks—each discipline has unique procedures. •Skill is determined by the crafterʼs level in the relevant craft and any perks or abilities theyʼve unlocked. This core formula keeps crafting consistent, no matter what you're building.
universality with discipline specific fl: The system is universal in structure but distinct in execution: •A blacksmith might manage forge heat and hammer strikes. •An alchemist balances reagent volatility and brewing timing. •An enchanter binds runes and manages charge capacity. •A tinker enhancing a vehicle might carefully install a speed mod while avoiding system overload. Each crafting discipline adds unique mechanics and checks that capture the essence of that craft without deviating from the shared foundation.
scaling difficulty progression: Crafting difficulty is determined by item complexity, and outcomes are influenced by: •Crafting DC: Based on item rarity and sophistication (e.g., DC 10 for simple tools, 20+ for legendary gear). •Skill Modifier: Based on your level in the relevant craft (e.g., blacksmithing, leatherworking, alchemy). •Tool & Material Bonuses: Using rare materials or masterwork tools boosts your chances. records.summary: Each material should have specific stats or traits that affect how it's used in the game. Some common properties include: - Hardness: A measure of the materialʼs resistance to damage or wear (important for armor, weapons, and durability). You can use a hardness scale (e.g., 1-10), where 1 is soft materials like cloth and 10 is materials like diamond. - Durability: Determines how long a material can last before it breaks or degrades. - Weight: Impacts movement speed, encumbrance, and portability. Heavier materials like iron may slow characters down or reduce mobility. - Flexibility: Important for materials used in tools or armor. More flexible materials might be better suited for specific types of items, such as leather for light armor. - Crafting Difficulty: How hard it is to work with the material. More exotic materials may require special skills, tools, or knowledge to craft effectively. - Magical Conduction: Determines if the material can hold enchantments or be used in spellcasting. Some materials may be better conduits for magic.
